name: Permissions-boundary-shaped policy: broad service access but no iam:PassRole / iam:* (no identity escalation)
note: A typical permissions-boundary body: broad workload services, deliberately no iam:PassRole and no IAM administration. Even read as an identity policy, it enables no privilege-boundary crossing.
rationale: A permissions boundary is an IAM policy that only CAPS the maximum permissions of an identity - it never grants on its own; effective permissions require an overlapping identity policy. Independent of that: this body contains no iam:PassRole and no iam:* action, so even evaluated as an identity policy it cannot pass a role to a workload (ec2:RunInstances / lambda:CreateFunction inside ec2:*/lambda:* are inert without iam:PassRole) and cannot administer IAM. Therefore no privilege-escalation and no DIRECT-IAM-ADMIN finding is warranted. The service wildcards are legitimately broad (WILDCARD-ACTION/WILDCARD-RESOURCE, high) but not critical escalation. Ref: AWS docs, 'Permissions boundaries for IAM entities'; and the requirement that PassRole-based escalation needs iam:PassRole present.
